html:
A battle fought on 28 October 312 just north of Rome, where the Via Flaminia crossed the Tiber on the Milvian Bridge. Constantine defeated his rival emperor Maxentius, who drowned in the river as his army broke.

Christian writers close to Constantine told of a sign before the battle. Lactantius says he was told in a dream to mark his soldiers' shields with a Christian symbol. Eusebius later wrote that Constantine saw a cross of light in the sky with the words "by this sign conquer". Historians argue over what he saw, but the victory linked him to the Christian God.

It made him master of the west and helped end the Tetrarchy. The next year came the Edict of Milan. The Senate put up the Arch of Constantine near the Colosseum to honour the win.
